llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (an agent-side security plugin) is plausible, but the SKILL.md makes unverifiable privacy/behavior claims and instructs the agent to install and rely on external plugin code that is not included — this mismatch and the sensitive key-handling deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim a runtime security plugin that contacts a central detection service and stores a local API key; the SKILL.md metadata lists network/storage permissions that match that purpose. However, the skill is instruction-only and does not include the plugin code it tells you to install (@openguardrails/moltguard), and the SKILL.md invokes the external openclaw CLI without declaring the openclaw binary as a required runtime dependency — this delegation reduces verifiability of the claims.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent/user to install an external plugin and to run commands that will display the local API key and agent ID (/og_status, /og_claim). The doc also tells the agent to read a sample file under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard/ to demonstrate detection. The SKILL.md asserts that only content hashes (no raw content/PII) are sent to the vendor, but there is no code bundled here to verify that behavior. Displaying API keys to the user is functional for 'claiming' but is a sensitive operation and could be abused or leaked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec or bundled code in this skill; instead it instructs the user/agent to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' which will fetch and execute external code at install time. Because the actual plugin implementation isn't included in the skill bundle, the SKILL.md's privacy/security claims cannot be validated from this package alone — installation will pull code from an external source whose provenance should be checked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables and does not require cloud credentials in the package metadata, which is proportionate. It does, however, create and store an API key locally (~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json) and provides commands that reveal that key and agent ID. Storing an API key locally is reasonable for a local protection agent, but exposing that key via commands increases the risk of accidental disclosure and should be considered before claiming/ sharing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or any elevated agent-wide privilege in the registry metadata. It describes storing its own credentials under the user's home directory, which is expected for a local plugin. It does not claim to modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is an instruction-only wrapper that tells the agent to install an external plugin and to register with a central service. Before installing: verify the plugin source (review the referenced GitHub repo and ensure the package name '@openguardrails/moltguard' comes from an official registry), inspect the plugin code to confirm that only hashes (and no raw content/PII/credentials) are transmitted, and confirm TLS and domain ownership for api.openguardrails.com. Be cautious about running commands that display the API key/agent ID (they can be copied or leaked). If you cannot audit the external plugin, consider running the installation in a sandboxed environment or decline installation.
